reason: The v0.1.33 isolated image passed both disk checks but failed owner assembly because the disposable RSA-3072 boot key was implicitly reused for PCR signing, which requires RSA-2048. Container failure then skipped ownership restoration and temporary cleanup raised PermissionError on root-owned Python bytecode.
changes: Generate a separate disposable RSA-2048 PCR authority for TPM-required canaries, while preserving RSA-3072 boot and evidence authorities.
Bind the PCR certificate during preflight and pass the matching ephemeral key only to isolated assembly; remove environment values afterward.
Restore assembly-directory ownership on success and failure without following payload symlinks, before temporary cleanup.
Disable Python bytecode writes for the isolated assembly entrypoint.
validation: Use actual OpenSSL keys and the owner PCR admission verifier; check distinct authorities and reject the old RSA-3072 PCR fallback.
Verify an optional-TPM fixture adds no PCR authority.
Verify failed container execution still restores ownership and preserves the original build error.
79 combined targeted tests pass; source/workflow checks and actual hosted qualification are required.
activation: Adopt the newly qualified immutable platform and exact workflow source in the private canary. Require successful actual image qualification, independent current-head human approval, then main image and immutable operational report before enabling its updater schedule.
approval: Independent current-head human approval after builds pass. This record grants no approval; canary output remains nondeployable and no production key is used.
